earlier_scan.note: Extinct pidgin known only from glossaries (Deen 1937) and minimal notes (Hualde 1984/1991); no stress description

sources.citation: Hualde, Jose Ignacio. 1991 [1984]. Icelandic Basque pidgin. ASJU 25(2): 427-437 (originally Journal of Basque Studies in America 5 (1984): 41-59). doi:10.1387/asju.8225
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; the paper is a syntactic/typological analysis of the handful of pidgin sentences in the second glossary. Only prosodic remark is that statements/questions/commands were 'possibly... distinguished by means of intonation only'.

sources.citation: Hualde, Jose Ignacio. 1991. Foreword to Glossaria duo Vasco-Islandica. ASJU 25(2): 317-319.
sources.note: Nothing; historical background on the manuscripts and Deen's edition.

sources.citation: Hualde, Jose Ignacio. 1991. Icelandic Basque pidgin (second OJS record of the same text, in ASJU Gehigarriak 23 = Bakker, Bilbao, Deen & Hualde, Basque Pidgins in Iceland and Canada).
sources.note: Same text as above; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Deen, Nicolaas G. H. 1937 [1991]. Glossaria duo Vasco-Islandica. Doctoral dissertation, Leiden (Amsterdam: H. J. Paris, 1937); Basque translation reprinted in ASJU 25(2): 321-426. doi:10.1387/asju.8223
sources.note: Nothing. Section I.E 'Fonetika arazoak' (phonetic questions) lists only segmental vowel/consonant substitutions in the Icelandic scribes' spellings of Basque words (a~e, e~i, etc.); no mention of accent/stress (grep for azentu/accent/Akzent/Betonung: zero hits).
